key_insight: Mach 8 compression-ramp simulations show that ablation interacts with boundary-layer streaks and influences perturbation evolution.
engineering_relevance: Predicting coupled surface recession and boundary-layer instability can support thermal-protection design for hypersonic vehicles.
method: Direct numerical simulation of Mach 8 flow over a 15° compression ramp.
Stability-informed perturbations applied to inert and low-temperature ablating surfaces.
Two independent solvers tested accelerated recession and higher-amplitude perturbations.
evidence_signal: The simulations reproduced characteristic experimental heating streaks on an inert ramp, while both solvers showed excellent agreement in heat fluxes, mass blowing rates, and recession patterns.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish experimental validation of the coupled ablating-flow predictions or applicability beyond this configuration.
paper_title: Transitional Fluid-Ablation Interactions on a Compression Ramp at Mach 8
